correctness.rationale: For every labelled biclique the induced-sum criterion is exactly the disjointness of the sets of selected row degrees and selected column degrees, including comparisons at zero-weight edges. Fewer than m selected edges leave degree-zero vertices in both parts; equality forces occupied fibres of size at least 2 on the larger side, giving a coefficient of \((e^x-x)^n\). In the balanced case the two star-center orientations are disjoint and complementation preserves all inequalities, yielding the full reciprocal symmetry. On \(K_{m,m+1}\), deficit-degree differences \(x_i-y_j\ne1\) exclude all one- and two-edge deletions and force three-edge deletions to be smaller-side stars, including the m=2 boundary. Exact integer brute-force tests on the actual standalone script exhaust 125006 binary masks plus additional extremal slices; the universal proof does not rely on finite data.

Published edge-irregularity deletion theorems check only retained edges and hence do not imply this all-original-edge count; existence algorithms and broad complexity results likewise supply no identified covering counting theorem. Relevant archive and primary-source searches found no claim that implies this precise classification. value.rationale: The minimum number of active weights and their full labelled and automorphism-type distribution are natural quantities in the binary neighbour-distinguishing edge-weighting problem, where local changes may destroy feasibility. The associated Stirling/partition census gives all optimal shapes across infinitely many bicliques, not a chosen numerical case; balanced complementation determines both extremes, and the consecutive-size family exhibits a sharp three-edge isolation threshold with an exact count. These are structural and enumeration statements beyond known existence and scalar deletion bounds; no general downstream application is asserted or needed.
